mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE rise > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or GDPC1 decline does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in one month signals strengthening economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase > 2% does not correlate with subsequent economic strength.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the CPIAUCSL is above 3% YoY, the expectation of future monetary tightening leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction between low FEDFUNDS and high CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in one month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or PAYEMS decrease > 100,000 does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in one month signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase > 10% does not correlate with subsequent consumer demand strength.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 1% YoY, the combination signals a restrictive monetary policy in a weak economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening in a weak economy
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction between high FEDFUNDS and low GDPC1 growth does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness.
